diagnosis.summary: order-api fast availability budget burn alert is not reproduced by the evidence: 5xx ratio is 0 for order-api and risk-engine, latency and request rates match the prior hour, and no workload or config change occurred before the incident. Cause is unknown.

probable_cause.statement: The evidence does not identify a cause. The error signal behind the budget burn is absent from the metrics provided.

supporting.statement: No new ReplicaSet or ConfigMap in sentinel-prod in the 09:01-09:30 window, so a deployment or config change is unlikely.
order-api 5xx ratio is 0 now and was 0 an hour earlier, so the metrics show no server errors.
order-api p95 latency and request rate are unchanged from an hour earlier, so no latency or load change is visible.
risk-engine latency, 5xx ratio and request rate are also unchanged, so the known downstream dependency shows no sign of stress.

missing_evidence: Which error signal drives the budget burn (for example, a non-5xx failure class, timeouts or client-side errors) and its burn-rate calculation over the alert window.
order-api and risk-engine logs and Kubernetes events for the alert window.
Metrics for other dependencies of order-api beyond risk-engine (database, cache, payment or downstream services).
Node and pod resource metrics (CPU, memory, restarts, OOM) for sentinel-prod.
Whether the burn is ongoing or already over, since the metrics pack shows only a point-in-time view at 09:31.

diagnosis.summary: order-api in sentinel-staging is returning 5xx (ratio 0.027 vs 0 an hour earlier) after two redeploys of the same image with a config change (faults config hash). Rollout revision 26 was aborted by a failed error-rate analysis; logs show injected 500 faults.

probable_cause.statement: The faults ConfigMap change (order-api-faults-c9gc88h72k to order-api-faults-5m8b668dd4) deployed with the same image caused order-api to return injected HTTP 500s, failing the error-rate analysis and aborting the rollout.

supporting.statement: Image digest was unchanged across the revisions, so the change was configuration, not a new image.
Argo CD synced staging to new commits right before each re-deployment, consistent with the config change being applied.
Pod startup and readiness probes failed with connection refused on order-api pods, consistent with the service not serving after the change.
Dependencies and other services look healthy: risk-engine error rate, latency and traffic are flat, so the failure is local to order-api.

missing_evidence: The contents of the faults ConfigMap diff are not in the pack, so the exact injected fault setting is unconfirmed.
No pod-level logs explaining why the startup probe failed on the new pods.
Whether the 500s are limited to a fault-injection path or affect all order-api requests is not shown beyond the 5xx ratio.
